text:
kevin_w: Ran an nsys trace on prod-replay with batch=16/seq=2048. Seeing a lot of churn around the KV cache apply kernel and some weird small kernels firing between big matmuls. attaching the key lines I noticed.

kevin_w: nsys snippet:
```
# 10:23:41.123  cudaDriver  kernel: transformer_attention_kv_apply   runtime  1.2ms  block_x  1024
# 10:23:41.125  cudaDriver  kernel: transformer_attn_matmul         runtime  0.9ms  block_x  1024
# 10:23:41.126  cudaDriver  kernel: kv_cache_reorg                   runtime  0.05ms
# 10:23:41.127  cudaDriver  kernel: small_elemwise                   runtime  0.02ms  (repeats)
```

priya_r: :eyes: do you have the nvtx timeline overlay? need to see ranges mapping to kernels.

kevin_w: sending timeline slice. I suspect our NVTX ranges are too fine-grained (per-op) so nsys shows a bunch of tiny ranges that make it hard to see high-level hotspots. also, after commit 9f3b2c2 (kv-batching) we started getting more small kernel handoffs. probably the batching heuristic triggers extra reorder work.

alex_m: agree. we added NVTX ranges for almost every internal op during the last refactor. nice for dev debugging but noisy for perf runs.

samira: two questions: 1) what's the overhead of pushing NVTX ranges per small op? 2) how do we keep enough context to map kernel -> logical request without drowning traces?

priya_r: measurements: on a microbenchmark, pushing ~200 nvtxPushRange/pop pairs per request added ~0.5-0.9ms CPU overhead and increased trace size ~3-4x. So not free.

alex_m: proposal: keep two levels of ranges only: request-level and stage-level. e.g. `NVTX range: req/<shortid>` then inside only a handful of stage ranges like `decode`, `kv_apply`, `batch_pack`, `kernel_launch`. that gives us mapping without micro-noise.

kevin_w: I like that. for mapping individual kernels we can still use kernel name labels in nsys and correlate by timestamp. no need to push a range for every tiny memcpy/elemwise.

samira: naming conventions: suggest `req:<shortid>:stage:<name>` (colon separated) so it's easy to grep and split fields. keep shortid to 8 chars. also add `meta:batch=<N>` as a single NVTX payload string for stage ranges so we can filter traces by batch size.

alex_m: implementation note: avoid allocating nvtx string objects per request. allocate a small pool of persistent c-strings for stage names and format a tiny per-request prefix into a stack buffer when needed. or better: push an integer id via `nvtxRangePushEx` with a pre-registered domain / message table. reduces GC and strdup churn.

priya_r: We should also support sampled NVTX: only emit request ranges for 1/N requests (configurable) during long-running perf traces. That keeps traces digestible.

kevin_w: followup: we found a perf regression where `kv_cache_reorg` happens more often than before because our batching heuristics pick mixes of seq lengths causing extra reorgs. I think we should: 1) log a metric when reorg occurs, 2) add a NVTX `stage` around the reorg (but only when tracing on), and 3) adjust heuristic to prefer grouping by kv-layout.

samira: +1. also add a small NVTX mark (not range) at the moment we decide batch composition. helps link decision -> kernel timeline. marks are cheap.

kevin_w: quick patch I sketched:
```
// pseudo
if (trace_enabled && sample_hit(req_id)) {
  char hdr[64]; snprintf(hdr, sizeof(hdr), "req:%08x:stage:kv_reorg:batch=%d", req_id_short, batch_size);
  nvtxRangePushA(hdr);
  do_kv_reorg();
  nvtxRangePop();
} else {
  do_kv_reorg();
}
```

alex_m: prefer domain-based approach: create domain once, and then use nvtxRangeId_t with `nvtxRangeStartEx`/`nvtxRangeEnd`. avoids string copies each time. we can maintain a small map from range id -> formatted string for trace post-processing.

priya_r: For postmortem trace analysis, make sure we emit a JSON sidecar mapping shortid -> full req metadata (model, batch, seq lenses). that lets perf engineers join traces to higher-level request shapes. store it alongside trace in s3.

deploy-bot: Trace artifact uploaded to gs://redwood-traces/1765223489/trace.nsys (size 184MB) :white_check_mark:

samira: next steps:
- adopt 2-level NVTX ranges in runtime (req + stage) and domain-based ids (alex)
- add cheap NVTX marks at batch-decision points (samira)
- enable sampled request ranges by default for long traces (priya)
- emit trace sidecar with per-req json for correlation (priya)
- tweak batching heuristic to prefer same-kv-layout grouping (kevin)

kevin_w: I'll prepare a small RFC/PR with benchmarks showing nvtx overhead and an example nsys timeline before/after. will include config knobs to toggle full per-op tracing for local dev.

samira: sounds good. if anyone wants to bike-shed naming, speak now :) :+1:

alex_m: tiny nit: use `req/` vs `req:`? I'm fine with either as long as we document it. prefer slashes for readability in nsys UI.

priya_r: let's pick `req/<shortid>/stage/<name>` then. agreed on shortid length 8. document in runtime/trace.md.

kevin_w: done, will link PR when ready. thanks all.
